title: Surgery and LITT seizure-outcome evidence, corrected (supersedes A0032-Report)
body:
## Scope and provenance
Corrected version of A0032-Report (failed R5 source check). No new searches. Every number below comes from one of the 14 EvidenceClaim artifacts committed in T0002 (A0017-A0030, all R5 gate = passed) or from the protocol (A0001); the claim id is given next to each number. The only count of sources stated here is the count of committed artifacts: 14 EvidenceClaims (A0017-A0030). All claims rest on abstracts or, for SLATE, a conference abstract page; no full texts were read (verification.access_level = abstract_only in every claim).

Study families (counted from the study_family_id field of the cited claims): the 14 claims carry 10 distinct family ids. Resection: fam-wiebe2001-tle-rct (A0017), fam-erset-nct00040326 (A0018), fam-dwivedi2017-aiims-peds-rct (A0019), fam-tellez2005-ma (A0020), fam-nhnn-london-adult-surgery-cohort (A0021). LITT: fam-litt-mtle-us-multicenter-wu2019 (A0022), fam-emory-slah (A0023), fam-slate-nct02844465 (A0024), fam-litt-pooled-meta-analyses (A0025, A0026, A0027, A0028, A0029). Guideline: fam-aes-cns-2026-guideline (A0030).

Protocol rules applied (A0001): follow-up >=12 months; mapping v1 'favourable' = Engel I or ILAE 1-2; paediatric-only cohorts recorded but analysed separately; same-patient publications count as one study family; no pooled estimate unless >=5 comparable studies.

## 1. Open resection

### 1a. Temporal resection vs medical therapy, RCTs (age >=12 or age not stated)
2 RCT families, n = 118 randomised (80 [A0017] + 38 [A0018]). Range: **58% [A0017] to 73% [A0018] free of disabling / awareness-impairing seizures at 1-2 years**, vs 8% [A0017] and 0/23 [A0018] on medical therapy.
- Wiebe 2001 (A0017): temporal-lobe epilepsy, n = 80 (40/40) [A0017]; age group not stated in the abstract (the claim headline's word 'adults' is not supported by the abstract; R5 note). 58% vs 8% free of seizures impairing awareness at 1 year, P<0.001 [A0017]; surgical adverse effects 10% [A0017].
- ERSET 2012 (A0018): early mesial TLE, age >=12 years (includes adolescents) [A0018], n = 38, halted early for slow accrual [A0018]. 11/15 (73%) vs 0/23 seizure free in year 2 [A0018]; memory decline in 4 (36%) after surgery [A0018].
- Endpoints are 'free of disabling seizures / seizures impairing awareness', an approximation to Engel I (favourable under mapping v1) [A0017, A0018].

### 1b. Paediatric-only RCT, mixed procedures (analysed separately per protocol)
- Dwivedi 2017 (A0019): age <=18 years, drug-resistant epilepsy of mixed aetiology, surgery 'appropriate to the underlying cause' (not temporal-specific) [A0019]; single centre, n = 116 (57/59) [A0019]. 77% vs 7% seizure free at 12 months, P<0.001 [A0019]; serious adverse events 33%, hemiparesis 26% [A0019]. Not pooled with 1a.

### 1c. Long-term observational evidence (labelled by procedure and population)
- Temporal resection, any age, cross-sectional definition: median long-term seizure-free proportion 66% across studies with mean/median follow-up >=5 years (Tellez-Zenteno 2005 MA, 83 studies, 0 RCTs) [A0020].
- Temporal lobe resection in mesial TLE, follow-up >24 months, pooled: 72.5% (65.6-78.5) seizure free (Ekman 2024 MA) [A0027]; age not stated in the claim.
- All procedures, adults (497 of 615 were anterior temporal resections) [A0021]: Kaplan-Meier continuous seizure freedom (apart from simple partial seizures) 52% (48-56) at 5 years and 47% (42-51) at 10 years; median follow-up 8 years (de Tisi 2011) [A0021]. This is not a temporal-only figure and uses a stricter time-to-first-seizure definition than A0020 [A0020, A0021].
- Extratemporal: median 46% occipital/parietal and 27% frontal (any age, >=5 y) [A0020]; extratemporal resection had higher recurrence than anterior temporal resection, HR 2.0 (1.1-3.6) [A0021].

Range for long-term temporal resection (temporal-specific figures only): **66% [A0020] to 72.5% [A0027]**. The all-procedure adult survival figures, 52% at 5 y and 47% at 10 y [A0021], are reported beside this range, not inside it.

## 2. Laser interstitial thermal therapy (LITT), mesial TLE
No RCT among the committed claims.

Primary cohorts (3 study families: wu2019, emory-slah, slate):
- Gross 2018, Emory (A0023): single-centre consecutive retrospective series, n = 58, MTLE [A0023]. 53.4% (40.8-65.7) Engel I at 1 year [A0023]; MTS 60.5% vs non-MTS 33.3% [A0023].
- SLATE (A0024): prospective single-arm multicentre device study, 21 US sites, 167 enrolled, 114 treated and followed 12 months [A0024]. Engel I 55.9% at 12 months (95% lower confidence limit 45.9%) [A0024]; qualifying AEs in 7.9% [A0024]. **Conference abstract only (AES 2024); no peer-reviewed results paper found by R1 or by R5's Europe PMC search. The AES abstract page states the study was funded by Medtronic** [A0024, R5 gate note]. Denominator for 55.9% not stated (to_verify) [A0024].
- Wu 2019 (A0022): 11-centre US retrospective cohort, n = 234, MTLE [A0022]; 58.0% Engel I at 1 and at 2 years [A0022]; age range and n analysed per timepoint not reported [A0022].

Pooled analyses (1 study family, fam-litt-pooled-meta-analyses; overlapping patients, not independent):
- Kerezoudis 2020 MA (A0025): 13 studies, 551 patients, TLE; seizure freedom 58% (54-62), MTS 66% (58-74); complications 17% [A0025]. **Follow-up not reported in the abstract** (>=12 mo compliance to_verify) [A0025].
- Chen 2023 IPD-MA (A0026): 46 studies, 450 patients, mixed DRE including paediatric and extratemporal cases; 240/415 (57.8%) seizure free at last follow-up [A0026]. **Median follow-up 19.0 months; individual patients may fall below 12 months, so protocol compliance is partial** [A0026]. CCM OR 7.97, MTS/atrophy OR 2.21 [A0026]; operative complications 8.5% [A0026].
- Ekman 2024 MA (A0027): LITT arm in MTLE, >24 months, 57.1% (51.2-62.7) [A0027].

LITT family count for this section: **4 study families** (fam-litt-mtle-us-multicenter-wu2019, fam-emory-slah, fam-slate-nct02844465, fam-litt-pooled-meta-analyses).

**LITT range used throughout this report: 53.4% [A0023] to 58.0% [A0022] Engel I at 12-24 months in mesial TLE, from the three primary-cohort families (A0022, A0023, A0024; SLATE 55.9% [A0024] lies inside).** The pooled MTLE/TLE values 57.1% [A0027] and 58% [A0025] fall inside this range but are not counted as additional independent evidence; A0026 (57.8%) is a mixed-DRE population and is not used to set the MTLE range.

## 3. LITT vs open surgery, non-randomised comparisons (all fam-litt-pooled-meta-analyses)
- Ekman 2024 (A0027), MTLE, >24 months: resection 72.5% vs LITT 57.1%, P<0.01 [A0027]; minor complications 9.9% vs 4.1% [A0027]. Compares pooled single-arm proportions.
- Pichardo-Rojas 2026 (A0028): 15 comparative cohort studies, 3873 patients, mixed ages and aetiologies [A0028]. LITT 52.5% vs open 67.1%, RR 0.78 (0.70-0.88) [A0028]; propensity-matched RR 0.85 (0.63-1.15), p=0.30, and TLE subgroup RR 0.88 (0.67-1.14), p=0.34, both not significant [A0028]; complication RR 0.54 [A0028]. **Follow-up not reported in the abstract** [A0028].
- Maroufi 2026 (A0029): nontumoral epilepsy, mixed ages, 11 comparative studies, 389 LITT vs 557 open [A0029]. Complete seizure freedom 53.7% vs 68.1%, RR 0.81, p=0.07 (not significant) [A0029]; complications 18.3% vs 30.0% [A0029]. **Follow-up not reported in the abstract** [A0029].

These three analyses share one study family and disagree on whether the gap persists after matching or within TLE [A0027, A0028, A0029]. LITT had fewer complications in all three [A0027, A0028, A0029].

## 4. Guideline
AES/CNS 2026 GRADE guideline (A0030): strong recommendation, moderate certainty, for ATL in MTLE at low cognitive risk; conditional, very low to low certainty, for SAH and LITT in MTLE and for neocortical resection; neurostimulation not addressed [A0030]. It synthesises the same primary studies and is not independent evidence [A0030].

## Bottom line (surgery/ablation arm)
- Temporal resection is the only intervention here with RCT support against medical therapy: 58% [A0017] to 73% [A0018] free of disabling seizures at 1-2 years (age >=12 or age not stated; 2 families, n = 118 [A0017, A0018]). The paediatric mixed-procedure RCT (77% at 12 months [A0019]) is kept separate per protocol.
- Long-term temporal resection: 66% [A0020] to 72.5% [A0027] seizure free (>=5 y cross-sectional and >24 mo pooled). Adult all-procedure survival-based continuous seizure freedom is lower: 52% at 5 y and 47% at 10 y [A0021]. Extratemporal resection is lower (46% / 27% [A0020]; HR 2.0 [A0021]).
- LITT in MTLE: 53.4% [A0023] to 58.0% [A0022] Engel I at 12-24 months from 3 primary-cohort families. One of them (SLATE, 55.9% [A0024]) is a Medtronic-funded conference abstract without a peer-reviewed results paper. No RCT.
- LITT vs open: numerically lower for LITT in unmatched pooled comparisons (52.5% vs 67.1% [A0028]; 57.1% vs 72.5% [A0027]); not significant in matched (RR 0.85 [A0028]) and TLE (RR 0.88 [A0028]) subgroups or in nontumoral epilepsy (p=0.07 [A0029]). LITT has fewer complications [A0027, A0028, A0029].
- Pooling: the protocol's >=5-comparable-study condition [A0001] is not met by independent families for any single procedure/population here (the LITT pooled analyses are one overlapping family). Report ranges, not a new pooled estimate.
- Under mapping v1 [A0001] the outcomes above map to 'favourable'; the Wiebe [A0017] and ERSET [A0018] endpoints are approximations to Engel I.

## Overlap notes
- A0025-A0029 share fam-litt-pooled-meta-analyses and likely include the Emory series (A0023) and possibly Wu 2019 (A0022) (to_verify) [A0022, A0025, A0026].
- SLATE shares sites with Wu 2019; patient overlap possible (to_verify) [A0022, A0024].
- Tellez-Zenteno 2005 may include earlier reports of the NHNN cohort behind de Tisi 2011 (to_verify) [A0020].
- The guideline synthesises the same primary studies [A0030].

## Indeterminate / not verified
- Full texts not read for any claim.
- Follow-up not reported in the abstracts of A0025, A0028 and A0029; A0026 median 19.0 months (partially compliant).
- A0017 age group not stated in the abstract; A0022 age range and per-timepoint n not reported.
- SLATE denominator for 55.9% not stated [A0024].
- Engel vs ILAE classes not separable from the abstracts for most meta-analyses [A0025, A0027, A0028, A0029].

## Changes vs A0032-Report
1. LITT family count corrected from 5 to 4, counted from study_family_id.
2. 'Temporal resection 47-77%' removed. Ranges are now labelled by population and procedure, the paediatric RCT is separate, and de Tisi is labelled all-procedure adults.
3. One LITT range (53.4-58.0%, endpoints from A0023 and A0022, with A0024 inside) is used in both section 2 and the bottom line.
4. The untraceable '15 sources opened' and the mention of an unopened, uncommitted MINE protocol are removed; only committed-artifact counts are stated.
5. R5 notes added: SLATE funding and no peer-reviewed paper; A0026 partial follow-up; A0025/A0028/A0029 follow-up not reported; A0017 age not stated.
6. Envelope --consumed now lists A0001 and A0017-A0030.
